findings.where: Ranking method section (four body paragraphs under one h2) and the Hostelworld comparison paragraph
findings.fault: Every paragraph in these sections is set at the same size and weight. No run-in lead, bold key phrase or subhead marks what each one is about. The section headed 'Ranking method' holds a paragraph about which reviews count, one about reward-code badges and one about the zero-review case. Nothing in the type signals these topics, so the only way to find one is to read from the top. On a phone that is about 30 lines of body text.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives doubting one claim, such as 'can a hostel pay to rank higher?' or 'what does a badge mean?'. They want to scan to that answer and check it. Undifferentiated prose makes the page feel like terms and conditions, not an open method, and the brief calls sterile or corporate the enemy.

findings.where: Page title 'How we rank' against the section headings ('Ranking method', 'Scoring method', 'Hostelworld, for comparison') and the lede, at both widths
findings.fault: The size steps are small. The h1 is only about a third larger than the h2s, and the lede below it is set large. On a nearly empty 1440 px screen the title doesn't stand clearly above the section heads. The page reads as flat document type with no single loud line.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand calls for 'loud moments, calm machine' with Quicksand 700 carrying the h1. A timid title on the page that holds the brand's main trust claim undersells it.
